title: What Is EMDR Therapy? A Clinical Psychologist Explains

sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊团指导、大师班、个性化指导、一份福南梅森（Fortnum and Mason）的美食礼品，以及限时的一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.zh: 谈到创伤，如果你之所以无法释怀并不是因为你软弱，那会是为什么呢？

sentences.en: What if it's because part of your brain is still responding as though the danger is happening right now?
sentences.zh: 如果是因为你大脑的一部分仍在做出反应，就好像危险正在此时此刻发生，又该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: In this episode, clinical psychologist, EMDR trainer, Dr. Alex Button, and I explore EMDR therapy, PTSD, trauma, grief, and how the brain can finally begin to learn.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我和临床心理学家、EMDR（眼动脱敏再加工）培训师亚历克斯·巴顿（Alex Button）博士将共同探讨EMDR疗法、PTSD、创伤、悲伤以及大脑最终如何开始重新学习。

sentences.en: That was then.
sentences.zh: 那是过去。

sentences.en: This is now.
sentences.zh: 这是现在。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《心理学其实》（Psychology Actually）。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologist, and I'm joined here today by a fellow qualified clinical psychologist, one that I do know rather well.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家，今天和我一起的是另一位合格的临床心理学家，也是一位我非常熟悉的人。

sentences.en: It's Dr. Alexandra Button.
sentences.zh: 她就是亚历罗克珊娜·巴顿博士。

sentences.en: Hi, Alex.
sentences.zh: 嗨，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: Hi, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 嗨，玛丽安。

sentences.en: Good to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Lovely to see you too.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Let's level people right at the start.
sentences.zh: 一开始，我们先向大家理清一些基本情况。

sentences.en: You are my EMDR supervisor, and you have been here for many years.
sentences.zh: 你是我的EMDR督导师，而且你已经担任这个角色很多年了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's because you are just amazing, Alex.
sentences.zh: 那是因为你实在是太棒了，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: But if people are watching this because they might be thinking, well, maybe I would want EMDR therapy for myself, or maybe I would want to train in it if I'm a clinician already.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果大家收看这个节目是因为他们在想：嗯，也许我自己会想做EMDR疗法，或者如果我本身就是临床医生，也许我想接受这方面的培训。

sentences.en: Could you give us a bit of an overview about what EMDR is?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们简单概述一下什么是EMDR吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So EMDR stands for eye movement desensitization and reprocessing.
sentences.zh: EMDR代表眼动脱敏再加工（eye movement desensitization and reprocessing）。

sentences.en: And it was developed in the 80s by a lady called Francine Shapiro, who had her own cancer diagnosis and was trying to work through that and process that.
sentences.zh: 它是由弗兰辛·夏皮罗（Francine Shapiro）女士在20世纪80年代开发的，当时她被诊断出患有癌症，并正试图克服和处理这一情况。

sentences.en: And she noticed that when she was going on a walk one day through the park, her eyes had been moving back and forth rapidly in a diagonal motion,
sentences.zh: 她注意到，有一天当她在公园散步时，她的眼睛在以对角线方向快速地来回移动，

sentences.en: and she felt less distressed about her diagnosis and what was happening for her.
sentences.zh: 她对自己的诊断以及所发生的事情感到没有那么痛苦了。

sentences.en: And then she consciously was thinking about what had been happening when she was walking, and that's how she noticed that her eyes had been moving back and forth really faSt.
sentences.zh: 然后，她有意识地思考她在散步时发生了什么，这就是她注意到自己的眼睛一直在非常快地来回移动的原因。

sentences.en: And then she started thinking about using that technique, I guess, for other difficulties that she was having.
sentences.zh: 接着，我想她开始考虑将这种技术用于她遇到的其他困难。

sentences.en: Not big traumas, just everyday kind of niggly things that were bothering her and realised it was having the same effect.
sentences.zh: 不是什么重大的创伤，只是一些困扰她的日常琐事，然后她发现这起到了同样的效果。

sentences.en: It was reducing her distress about events.
sentences.zh: 它减轻了她对事件的痛苦感受。

sentences.en: And she then went on to do proper research with initially Vietnam veterans, survivors of sexual assault, and had the same results.
sentences.zh: 随后，她继续进行了真正的研究，最初是以越战老兵和性侵幸存者为对象，并取得了同样的结果。

sentences.en: But because she was then doing the eye movements with other people, she was using her hand to direct their eyes.
sentences.zh: 但因为她当时在和别人一起做眼动，她用手来引导他们的眼睛。

sentences.en: And so that's where eye movement came from.
sentences.zh: 这就是“眼动”这个名字的由来。

sentences.en: It was originally a therapy treatment for PTSD and still is.
sentences.zh: 它最初是针对PTSD的治疗方法，现在依然是。

sentences.en: It's in the NICE guidelines for PTSD.
sentences.zh: 它被列入了NICE（英国国家健康与临床优化研究所）关于PTSD的指南中。

sentences.en: But actually what we know now is EMDR works for lots and lots of different presenting issues because so many different presenting issues have an underpinning of trauma around them.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们现在知道EMDR适用于许多不同的呈现问题，因为有那么多不同的呈现问题周围都存在着创伤的根基。

sentences.en: So what EMDR does, I mean, there's lots of different neurobiology and explanations for it.
sentences.zh: 所以EMDR的作用是——我的意思是，有很多不同的神经生物学解释。

sentences.en: But in a nutshell, for laypeople, it's a way of like, if you think of a computer that's got lots of like fragments, I guess, of sort of information in there that is not,
sentences.zh: 但简而言之，对于外行人来说，这就好比，如果你把大脑想象成一台电脑，里面有很多碎片的、某种程度上的信息，这些信息并没有……

sentences.en: hasn't been made sense of properly.
sentences.zh: 没有被正确地理解和消化。

sentences.en: It's kind of the same with traumatic experiences,
sentences.zh: 这有点类似于创伤经历，

sentences.en: that the brain can't make sense of those experiences necessarily in the same way that it would with everyday events like having your breakfast, going to the shops, etc.
sentences.zh: 大脑无法像对待吃早餐、去商店等日常事件那样，去自然地理解这些经历。

sentences.en: You know, when something happens to you that overwhelms your brain's natural healing capacity and an inherent capacity to make sense of something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当发生了一些事情，超出了你大脑的自然治愈能力以及理解某事的固有能力时。

sentences.en: We get like a backlog, if you like, of information, and that might be smells, sounds, thoughts, feelings, body sensations, like fragments of the experience from the time.
sentences.zh: 如果我们这样比喻的话，我们就会积压大量的信息，这可能是气味、声音、想法、感觉、身体感受，就像当时经历的碎片一样。

sentences.en: And those don't get made sense of in the same way as they normally would.
sentences.zh: 而这些并没有像平常那样被正确理解。

sentences.en: So what happens is people end up with a bit of a backlog, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，人们最终会积压一些东西。

sentences.en: Like I say to my clients, it's like if you imagine a cupboard in your mind that we've just stuffed everything in in order to get on with life.
sentences.zh: 就像我对我的客户所说的那样，这就像如果你想象你脑海中有一个柜子，为了继续生活，我们把所有东西都塞了进去。

sentences.en: And then things in the everyday life will be will trigger that door of that cupboard to sort of fling open and bits will spill out.
sentences.zh: 然后日常生活中的某些事情就会触发那个柜子的门猛然打开，里面的碎片就会倾泻而出。

sentences.en: And then people re-experience those fragments of information as if they're happening again.
sentences.zh: 接着，人们会重新体验那些信息碎片，就好像它们正在再次发生一样。

sentences.en: So a lot of my clients will say, I know it was a year ago, a month ago, 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的许多客户会说：“我知道那是是一年前、一个月前、十年前发生的。”

sentences.en: But when it when I get triggered back into it, it feels like it's happening again.
sentences.zh: 但是当我被触发重新陷入其中时，感觉就像它正在发生一样。

sentences.en: And that's because those fragments of information haven't been date stamped and filed in the other part of the brain.
sentences.zh: 那是因为那些信息碎片没有像日常事件那样被加上日期戳并归档到大脑的其他部分中。

sentences.en: Like they would for everyday events.
sentences.zh: 就像日常事件那样。

sentences.en: So EMDR, there's like I said, there's different explanations of it, but it's kind of like rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以EMDR——就像我说的，对它有不同的解释——但它有点像快速眼动睡眠。

sentences.en: People think it's sort of like rapid eye movement sleep where your brain is sort of defragging, if you like,
sentences.zh: 人们认为它有点像快速眼动睡眠，通过眼睛来回的快速运动，你的大脑在夜间整理，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: backlogs of information through the night with the rapid movement of the eyes back and forth.
sentences.zh: 清理积压的信息。

sentences.en: And there are other theories like taxing the working memory.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的理论，比如占用工作记忆。

sentences.en: So you can't when you bring up a distressing event and you are then part of your attention is taken up attending to something else.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你浮现出一个痛苦的事件时，你的一部分注意力就被占用去关注别的事情了。

sentences.en: Like the presence of the here and now or the eye movements or some people have like headphones on that bleep or click alternately or they might have buzzers or they might tap themselves.
sentences.zh: 比如此时此地的存在、眼动，或者有些人戴着交替发出哔哔声或咔哒声的耳机，或者他们可能有蜂鸣器，或者他们可能会自己敲击身体。

sentences.en: We see videos of this online.
sentences.zh: 我们在网上看到了这种视频。

sentences.en: So that bilateral stimulation not only kind of activates and jumpstarts this inherent natural healing capacity,
sentences.zh: 因此，这种双侧刺激不仅能激活并启动这种内在的自然治愈能力，

sentences.en: but it's also somewhat of another thing your brain is having to give up some bandwidth to attend to.
sentences.zh: 而且也在某种程度上占据了你大脑的一部分带宽去关注其他事情。

sentences.en: So then you've got a competing demand on your working memory, which can take the heat out of the distressing information.
sentences.zh: 所以此时你的工作记忆面临着竞争性的需求，这可以消除痛苦信息中的热度。

sentences.en: But having said that, all of that is happening within the context of, hopefully for people, a sound therapeutic relationship.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，所有这一切都是在一种良好的治疗关系背景下进行的，这对于人们来说是希望所在的。

sentences.en: So they are bringing to mind the difficult event in the safety of sitting with somebody who's able to support them through it,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在能够陪伴并支持他们度过难关的人的陪伴下，在安全的环境中回想困难的事件，

sentences.en: which is very different to having a flashback and the stuff coming out the cupboard in the mind and trying to manage it themselves.
sentences.zh: 这与经历闪回、脑海柜子里的东西涌出并试图自己去应对是有很大区别的。

sentences.en: So that's like the lay person's version of what EMDR is.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是外行人版本的EMDR是什么。

sentences.en: That's how I would, but obviously when I'm training, I go into a lot more detail than that.
sentences.zh: 这就是我将要表达的，但显然当我进行培训时，我会讲得比这详细得多。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Thanks, Alex.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: That was really, really helpful.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有帮助。

sentences.en: I think I'm right in saying that Shapiro said if she was renaming it again now, when she's no longer with us, she's passed away, I think, hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 我想我没记错的话，夏皮罗曾说过，如果她现在重新给它命名的话——她已经不在了，她已经去世了，我想是这样的吧？

sentences.en: But if she was going to be naming it again,
sentences.zh: 但如果她要重新命名它的话，

sentences.en: she perhaps wouldn't call it eye movement because could you tell us then why we've got all these different ways that we can can kind of use it, not just with eyes?
sentences.zh: 她可能不会称之为“眼动”，因为你能告诉我们为什么我们可以用所有这些不同的方式来使用它，而不仅仅是通过眼睛吗？

sentences.en: What's the theory behind that?
sentences.zh: 这背后的理论是什么？

sentences.en: Well, so it started with eye movements because that's what she noticed in herself was her eyes were moving rapidly back and forth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是从眼动开始的，因为那是她在自己身上注意到的现象，即她的眼睛在快速地来回移动。

sentences.en: And certainly the initial like pilot studies in the MDR in the 80s, it was all and and for a long time into the 90s, it was all sort of eye movement.
sentences.zh: 当然，80年代EMDR最初的类似试点研究，以及在90年代很长一段时间里，全都是关于眼动的。

sentences.en: So the gold standard, the research is around eye movements.
sentences.zh: 所以黄金标准，相关的研究都是围绕眼动的。

sentences.en: However, what what we now know is that tapping ourselves left and right and any form of bilateral stimulation,
sentences.zh: 然而，我们现在所知道的是，左右敲击我们自己以及任何形式的双侧刺激，

sentences.en: anything that is stimulating the brain left and right and left and right.
sentences.zh: 任何能够左右、左右刺激大脑的事物。

sentences.en: Whilst someone is holding in mind the difficult event that happened for them and in the safety of the therapeutic relationship also will have the same kind of effect.
sentences.zh: 当某人在脑海中记着发生给他们的困难事件，并且在安全的治疗关系中时，也会产生同样的效果。

sentences.en: And this is why she said she wishes she hadn't called it eye movements,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么她说她希望自己当初没有把它命名为眼动，

sentences.en: because what people went on to find out that is the tapping alternately or people holding buzzers alternately or the auditory.
sentences.zh: 因为人们后来发现交替敲击、或者人们交替拿着蜂鸣器、或者听觉刺激也有用。

sentences.en: But also there are research studies.
sentences.zh: 而且还有研究论文。

sentences.en: There was a lot of stuff happening in Cardiff University over the last few years with veterans who were on running machines.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，卡迪夫大学（Cardiff University）对在跑步机上的退伍军人做了很多研究。

sentences.en: That was their bilateral stimulation.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的双侧刺激。

sentences.en: And certainly clinicians that work with children and adolescents are very creative in how they're doing the BLS.
sentences.zh: 当然，与儿童和青少年合作的临床医生在如何进行BLS（双侧刺激）方面非常有创意。

sentences.en: You know, they've got children hopping from one foot to another or doing all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们让孩子们单脚跳跃或者做各种各样的动作。

sentences.en: And it will have the same.
sentences.zh: 这也会起到同样的效果。

sentences.en: It will be stimulating the brain left, right, left, right in the same way.
sentences.zh: 它会以同样的方式刺激大脑左、右、左、右。

sentences.en: But the research literature is obviously much more around very clinically in a room, you know, with eye movements or with the tappers or the buzzers.
sentences.zh: 但研究文献显然更多地集中在非常临床的房间里，你知道的，通过眼动、敲击器或蜂鸣器。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这太有趣了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I think lots of people who perhaps don't work in this space don't necessarily realise that in order for me to wave my broken right hand at you,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为许多不从事这个领域工作的人不一定意识到，为了让我向你挥动我受伤的右手，

sentences.en: that's actually the left side of my brain that's doing that.
sentences.zh: 实际上是我大脑的左侧在做这件事。

sentences.en: And then for me to point to the left side of my brain with my left hand, that's the right side of my brain that's doing that.
sentences.zh: 然后为了让我用左手指向我大脑的左侧，那是我大脑的右侧在做这件事。

sentences.en: So what we're looking to do and what we do manage to do with EMDR is we're activating both hemispheres of the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们寻求做的事情，也是我们通过EMDR成功做到的事情，就是激活大脑的两个半球。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's there's actually, you know, so the brain is so complex, we will never know.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，你知道的，大脑是如此复杂，我们永远不会完全了解。

sentences.en: We will never know exactly what EMDR is doing, despite all the MRI studies and brain scan imaging, you know, scanning studies that happen.
sentences.zh: 尽管有那么多的MRI研究和脑扫描成像研究，我们永远不会确切知道EMDR究竟在做什么。

sentences.en: We will never know for sure what the exact mechanisms of EMDR are.
sentences.zh: 我们永远无法百分之百确定EMDR的确切机制是什么。

sentences.en: But there is plenty of literature out there describing different mechanisms of action.
sentences.zh: 但有大量的文献描述了不同的作用机制。

sentences.en: But I think therapists and clients get very hung up on what is it because of the eye movements.
sentences.zh: 但我认为治疗师和客户往往过于纠结于它之所以有效是因为眼动。

sentences.en: And then that makes them curious.
sentences.zh: 然后这让他们感到好奇。

sentences.en: Well, how is that having an effect?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这到底是怎么产生效果的呢？

sentences.en: And absolutely right to be curious about that.
sentences.zh: 对此感到好奇是绝对正确的。

sentences.en: But we also don't ask all those questions of compassion focused therapy or CBT or ACT.
sentences.zh: 但我们不会对慈悲焦点疗法（CFT）、CBT（认知行为疗法）或ACT（接纳承诺疗法）提出所有这些问题。

sentences.en: You know, we don't ask those same questions about talking.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们不会对谈话提出同样的问题。

sentences.en: We don't think about what's happening in the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去想大脑里发生了什么。

sentences.en: But I think I think it would be safe to say the brain is so complex that we will never know 100 percent what is happening exactly in EMDR and what the mechanisms of action are.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，大脑是如此复杂，我们可以肯定地说，我们永远无法百分之百确切地知道EMDR中究竟发生了什么以及作用机制是什么。

sentences.en: But there are so many different theories and so many imaging studies that will show differences in parts of the brain that are lit up, if you like.
sentences.zh: 但有如此多的不同理论和成像研究，展示了大脑中被点亮的不同区域的差异。

sentences.en: If you were to scan the brain, lit up pre and post EMDR therapy for things like PTSD.
sentences.zh: 如果你对大脑进行扫描，会发现针对PTSD等问题进行EMDR治疗前后，大脑被点亮的部分是有差异的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's impossible to say for sure.
sentences.zh: 所以要确切地说是不可能的。

sentences.en: But it's definitely it's not necessarily as clear cut as left and right, because there will be multiple areas of the brain involved in those processes during the EMDR therapy.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对不一定像左右之分那么明确，因为在EMDR治疗过程中的那些活动中会涉及大脑的多个区域。

sentences.en: So helpful.
sentences.zh: 太有帮助了。

sentences.en: Thank you, Alex.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: And so if if someone's thinking, well, what kind of things could this be used for and what what symptoms might someone be experiencing?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果有人在想，这可以用于什么样的事情，以及人们可能会经历什么症状？

sentences.en: I guess, for example, if we if we spoke about someone that had been involved in a multi car traffic accident,
sentences.zh: 我想，举个例子，如果我们谈论一个遭遇过多车相撞交通事故的人，

sentences.en: what kind of things might they be experiencing and how might EMDR be helpful?
sentences.zh: 他们可能会经历什么样的事情，EMDR又是如何提供帮助的呢？

sentences.en: So I've I've just given you a random thing so that you're not accidentally giving us client.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚才随口举了一个随机的例子，这样你就不会不小心给我们提供某个真实的客户。

sentences.en: I know you're very good at client protection, but no one client would ever want to think that they were being identified.
sentences.zh: 我知道你非常擅长客户隐私保护，但没有哪个客户会愿意觉得自己被识别出来。

sentences.en: So I've just picked something random.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是随便选了一些东西。

sentences.en: Typical scenario that we might exactly.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们可能会遇到的典型场景。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: And so, yeah,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，

sentences.en: it's very common that we were especially in them through insurance companies and stuff that therapists will have people referred to them who've been in some kind of accident,
sentences.zh: 治疗师通过保险公司等渠道接到遭遇某种事故（通常是交通事故）的转诊客户是非常常见的。

sentences.en: usually a traffic accident.
sentences.zh: 但这也可能是与工作相关的事情。

sentences.en: But it might be a work related thing.
sentences.zh: 但以你的例子来说，我想你刚才暗示的是典型的PTSD类型的症状表现。

sentences.en: But to use your example, I think what you were alluding to, though, is kind of the typical PTSD type presentation.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为临床医生，在我们所谓的单纯性PTSD中，我们通常要寻找三组不同的症状，其中之一就是重新体验症状。

sentences.en: So we have sort of three different sets of symptoMs. Typically, we're looking out for as clinicians in in what we call simple PTSD, which are the re experiencing symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以某人可能会经历闪回，这就像是对事件的字面上的重新经历。

sentences.en: So somebody might be having flashbacks, which is like literal reliving of the event.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉就像它正在再次发生一样。

sentences.en: So it feels as if it's happening again.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会有闯入性记忆，这略有不同，因为当事人仍然会有现在是2026年的感觉。

sentences.en: They might be having intrusive memories, which are slightly different in that they still have person will still have a sense of it being 2026.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的是高度唤醒状态，感觉就像……所以他们有点在经历双重的状态。

sentences.en: But they there's the hyper arousal that comes with that is feeling like so they're kind of experiencing both.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意这么说的话，他们知道自己身处现在，但他们确实在字面上体验到了当时的一些气味、声音等等。

sentences.en: If you like that, they know they're in there now, but they are literally experiencing some of the smells, sounds, et cetera, from the time.
sentences.zh: 这有一点微小的区别。

sentences.en: That's a slight difference.
sentences.zh: 然后另一种典型的重新体验症状是噩梦。

sentences.en: And then the other typical kind of re experiencing symptom is nightmares.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们会报告说做了噩梦，这可能是对事件的字面重新经历，或者是一个主题的噩梦。

sentences.en: So people will report having bad dreams and that might be like a literal reliving of the event or it will be on a theme.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是一个被困住而无法逃脱的梦，这可能就是车祸中发生的情况。

sentences.en: So it might be a trapped and can't get out kind of dream, which might be what happened in the car crash.
sentences.zh: 但梦中可能没有汽车，或者他们字面上就是在做自己被困在汽车里的噩梦。

sentences.en: But the dream might not be a car or it might be that they're literally having a nightmare of having been trapped in the car.
sentences.zh: 这真是太生动了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So those are the re experiencing symptoMs. And then people will often have what we call hyper arousal symptoms as well, which is where the threat system is very on.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是再次经历症状。然后人们通常还会有我们所说的高警觉症状，也就是威胁系统处于高度开启状态。

sentences.en: So they're looking out for stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直在警惕着周围的事物。

sentences.en: They're very vigilant.
sentences.zh: 他们非常警觉。

sentences.en: They don't want to get back in a car.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不想再坐进汽车里。

sentences.en: They're very triggered by like the sound of braking or sirens or it's kind of everything's very on is one way I would describe it,
sentences.zh: 比如听到刹车声或警笛声，他们就会被狠狠触发，或者说可以用“整个人处于高度紧绷状态”来形容，

sentences.en: whether that's all the senses or the person's emotions are very heightened.
sentences.zh: 无论是所有的感官还是个人的情绪都高度亢奋。

sentences.en: So they might be very afraid, big start or response, easily jumpy, panicky or angry.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能会非常害怕，容易被吓到，一惊一乍，容易大惊小怪、慌乱或愤怒。

sentences.en: Some people are very angry or it might be a big old mix of those everything being on stuff.
sentences.zh: 有些人非常愤怒，或者这可能是所有这些紧绷状态的大杂烩。

sentences.en: And then we have our hypo arousal or numbing or avoidance set of symptoms that we call it,
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有所谓的低警觉、麻木或回避类症状，

sentences.en: which is kind of the other end of the spectrum where the threat system can't stay on all of the time.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是光谱的另一端，因为威胁系统不可能一直保持开启状态。

sentences.en: So then people might find that their system goes the other way and almost like detaches from stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能会发现他们的系统走向了另一个极端，几乎像是与外界切断了联系。

sentences.en: So some people will describe having no feelings about anything, including good feelings, like they've lost all feeling for everything.
sentences.zh: 因此，有些人会描述说自己对任何事情都没有感觉，包括好的感觉，就像他们失去了对一切事物的感知一样。

sentences.en: They just don't care anymore about stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不再在乎任何事情了。

sentences.en: They feel very disconnected from people that they used to be really close to.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己与曾经非常亲密的人之间产生了很强的疏离感。

sentences.en: They will sometimes have stopped doing activities that they used to like to do.
sentences.zh: 他们有时甚至会停止做那些曾经喜欢做的事情。

sentences.en: It's kind of a real shutting down and loss of interest in life, which can look like depression.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是一种真正的自我关闭和对生活失去兴趣，看起来可能很像抑郁症。

sentences.en: And also the hyper arousal in PTSD can look like anxiety.
sentences.zh: 而且，创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）中的高警觉也可能表现得像焦虑症。

sentences.en: So sometimes people who should have been diagnosed with PTSD will come away from a GP surgery with diagnoses of anxiety and depression often.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时本该被诊断为PTSD的人，从全科医生诊所出来时，往往带着焦虑症和抑郁症的诊断。

sentences.en: And it's only when you meet them and you start asking them, well, when did you become depressed or when did you become anxious?
sentences.zh: 只有当你与他们交流，开始问他们：“嗯，你是什么时候开始感到抑郁或焦虑的？”

sentences.en: And they essentially tell a trauma story.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就会讲出一个创伤的故事。

sentences.en: So PTSD is like the common thing that people would think of EMDR as being used for.
sentences.zh: 所以，PTSD就像是人们一想到EMDR（眼动脱敏再加工疗法）就会联想到的最常见用途。

sentences.en: And it's certainly in the PTSD NICE guidelines for treatment for adults and children.
sentences.zh: 而且它绝对被写进了NICE（英国国家卫生与临床优化研究所）关于成人和儿童PTSD治疗的指南中。

sentences.en: But what I've noticed is, and I said this earlier, so many different presenting conditions often have trauma in the background,
sentences.zh: 但我注意到的是，正如我刚才所说，许多不同表现形式的病症背后往往都有创伤的影子，

sentences.en: whether that's big trauma like something like a baby loss or a sexual assault or an accident or an injury of some kind.
sentences.zh: 无论是像失去婴儿、性侵、事故或某种身体伤害这样的大型创伤。

sentences.en: But lots of other people have the less obvious traumas and they might sit in front of me and say, well, but I haven't had trauma, Alex.
sentences.zh: 但许多其他人经历的是没那么明显的创伤，他们可能会坐在我面前说：“嗯，可是我没有经历过创伤啊，亚历克斯。”

sentences.en: And then they tell me about long histories of being bullied at school, for example,
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会向我讲述他们长期在学校遭受霸凌的经历，

sentences.en: or parents that were super busy or they might have had a sibling with like a lot of medical conditions.
sentences.zh: 或者是父母忙得不可开交，或者他们可能有一个有许多健康状况的兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: And actually the parents were so occupied necessarily dealing with the sibling that actually they didn't particularly get very seen and heard.
sentences.zh: 事实上，父母由于必须照顾那个兄弟姐妹而耗费了大量精力，以至于他们自己并没有真正被看到和听到。

sentences.en: And it's not the parents fault.
sentences.zh: 这并不是父母的错。

sentences.en: It just is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And so what I'm looking for in the therapy I do with people and certainly masses, as you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，我在对人们进行的治疗中寻找的，当然正如你所知，在我督导的大量案例中，

sentences.en: of what I supervise isn't the big obvious trauma where people go, well, I haven't been a soldier and I haven't been in a tsunami or I haven't been in a plane crash.
sentences.zh: 并不是那种每个人都会觉得“我没有当过士兵，没有经历过海啸，也没有遭遇过空难，所以我没有创伤”的明显大创伤，而是我们所说的小t创伤，

sentences.en: So I haven't got trauma, but actually we're looking at what we call the small T traumas for people, which is like the drip, drip, drip of the not so obvious stuff,
sentences.zh: 也就是那些不那么明显的事情带来的点点滴滴的积累，

sentences.en: but it takes its toll.
sentences.zh: 但它却会付出代价。

sentences.en: And that can show up as like really low self-esteem, feeling really rubbish about themselves, feeling depressed, lacking confidence or might show up as body dysmorphia.
sentences.zh: 这可能会表现为非常低的自尊心、觉得自己一文不值、感到抑郁、缺乏自信，或者表现为身体变形恐惧症。

sentences.en: There's something wrong with me.
sentences.zh: 觉得自己身上有什么毛病。

sentences.en: You know, people that have been bullied for their looks, for example, or it might show up as an eating disorder or OCD is a common presentation that I see.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如因为外表而被霸凌的人，或者它可能表现为进食障碍，强迫症（OCD）也是我经常看到的一种病症。

sentences.en: Not just in my own therapy service, but in all the supervisees that I have.
sentences.zh: 不仅在我自己的治疗服务中，在我所有的督导对象中也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, it takes takes many different forms, but there's often trauma underpinning these conditions.
sentences.zh: 是的，它有很多不同的形式，但这些病症背后往往都有创伤在支撑。

sentences.en: Yeah, there really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I was just thinking as you were speaking, like I obviously do a lot of work for grief and people obviously can be completely destroyed by grief, understandably so.
sentences.zh: 刚才听你说话时我在想，我显然做了很多关于悲伤的工作，人们显然会被悲伤彻底摧毁，这是完全可以理解的。

sentences.en: And I often think with people about when it comes to grief, it's whether we can help you separate the grief from the trauma.
sentences.zh: 对于悲伤，我经常考虑的是，我们能否帮你把悲伤和创伤剥离开来。

sentences.en: If we can get the trauma bits to lay flat and they were like, well, I'm never going to feel any different to this.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能让创伤的部分平复下来，而他们却觉得：“嗯，我的感觉永远不会有什么不同了。”

sentences.en: And I'm like, I often will kind of think about when I lost my dad in 2017, it all felt like grief.
sentences.zh: 我会经常回想2017年我父亲去世的时候，一切感觉都像是悲伤。

sentences.en: But actually, over time, I began to think about key painful bits.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，随着时间的推移，我开始想起一些关键的痛苦片段。

sentences.en: So, for example, there was a bit where he was trying to walk to the toilet with the help of a nurse who thought that he was stronger than he was.
sentences.zh: 比如，有一个片段是他试图在护士的帮助下走到洗手间去，那个护士以为他比实际上更有力气。

sentences.en: And then he kind of faltered and kind of went to fall over.
sentences.zh: 然后他有点踉跄，差一点摔倒。

sentences.en: That really wasn't lying flat with me, Alex.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，那个片段在我心里真的没有平复下来。

sentences.en: And it's because with hindsight, that's not grief.
sentences.zh: 那是因为事后诸葛亮地来看，那不是悲伤。

sentences.en: That's that's a trauma, a trauma aspect.
sentences.zh: 那是创伤，是创伤的一个方面。

sentences.en: So when I'm working with people, we'll be like, let's deal with the trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以当我与人们工作时，我们会说：让我们来处理创伤吧。

sentences.en: And often they will say, I'm actually happy to keep the grief because that feels important to me.
sentences.zh: 通常他们会说：其实我很乐意保留这份悲伤，因为这对我来说很重要。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Like you, I work with a lot of grief.
sentences.zh: 和你一样，我也处理过很多悲伤的案例。

sentences.en: If sadly, life is difficult for people, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 如果说得悲伤一点，生活对人们来说真的很艰难，不是吗？

sentences.en: People lose people in like for you and I very drawn out experiences of losing a loved one.
sentences.zh: 人们会失去亲人，就像对你我而言，那是失去挚爱经历的漫长拉锯战。

sentences.en: But for other people, it's it's literally sudden and both have different trauma aspects to them, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但对其他人来说，这简直是突如其来的，两者都有不同的创伤层面，对吧？

sentences.en: But like you say, you know, I think some people worry clinicians particularly will say, well,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，你知道，我认为有些人会担心，尤其是临床医生会说，

sentences.en: I can't I can't do EMDR with this person because they've only just lost this person and they need to wait several months to see.
sentences.zh: 我不能对这个人进行EMDR治疗，因为他们才刚刚失去亲人，他们需要等待几个月再看。

sentences.en: And actually, that's a myth.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，这是一种迷思。

sentences.en: Like you've said, it's the EMDR will be treating the trauma of what's happened to them.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，EMDR治疗的是他们所经历的事情带来的创伤。

sentences.en: EMDR will not remove a normal grieving process.
sentences.zh: EMDR不会消除正常的悲伤过程。

sentences.en: So I certainly have a number of supervisees say, well, I can't start yet because I don't want to disrupt their grieving process.
sentences.zh: 所以我的确听到过一些督导对象说：“嗯，我还不能开始，因为我不想打乱他们的悲伤过程。”

sentences.en: And I'm like, EMDR won't.
sentences.zh: 而我的回答是：EMDR不会的。

sentences.en: EMDR will only remove the the bit that shouldn't be there.
sentences.zh: EMDR只会消除那些不该存在的部分。

sentences.en: EMDR will not remove something normal, rational, valid.
sentences.zh: EMDR不会消除正常、理性、有效的东西。

sentences.en: You know, so whilst we will process with people to take away the trauma, like you say, like, let's iron out the hills, if you like, or the mountains in the story,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以虽然我们会和人们一起处理以消除创伤，就像你说的，让我们像熨平故事中的小山丘或者高山一样，

sentences.en: then actually they will still have the bumps and the ups and downs of the grief.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他们仍然会经历悲伤中的磕磕绊绊、起起伏伏。

sentences.en: Of course, they will, because that's normal.
sentences.zh: 他们当然会的，因为那是正常的。

sentences.en: But what I've seen happen with people is, especially with traumatic grief, they will come like really traumatised by what's happened.
sentences.zh: 但我看到人们身上发生的情况是，特别是在创伤性悲伤中，他们来到时会因为发生的事情而受到巨大的创伤。

sentences.en: They are either completely flooded all of the time or they've shut down and they aren't talking to anyone about it.
sentences.zh: 他们要么整天完全处于情绪泛滥状态，要么已经自我封闭，不跟任何人谈论这件事。

sentences.en: They won't think about it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不去想它。

sentences.en: They're massively avoidant to the point where it's causing a problem in their lives, obviously.
sentences.zh: 他们极度回避，以至于显然已经给他们的生活造成了问题。

sentences.en: And what I've always, always seen with grief is when we process the trauma, what will happen is your connection to that loved one that is around as a traumatic event,
sentences.zh: 而且我在悲伤治疗中一直、总是看到的是，当我们处理创伤时，会发生什么呢？你与那位作为创伤事件存在的挚爱的联结，

sentences.en: that will get removed.
sentences.zh: 那个创伤会被移除。

sentences.en: And then what people get, what comes in its place is the good memories come back.
sentences.zh: 然后取而代之的是，美好的记忆会重新涌现。

sentences.en: Like they don't lose a connection.
sentences.zh: 就像他们并没有失去这种联结一样。

sentences.en: I think a lot of clinicians and clients worry, well, if I process this, then I've lost them.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多临床医生和客户会担心：“如果我处理了这个，那么我就失去他们了。”

sentences.en: They're gone completely.
sentences.zh: “他们彻底消失了。”

sentences.en: And that has never happened in all the people I've worked with.
sentences.zh: 而在我合作过的所有人当中，这种情况从来没有发生过。

sentences.en: Actually, they get the good stuff about the person back.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们找回了关于那个人的美好回忆。

sentences.en: They get a reconnection with the person that isn't about trauma.
sentences.zh: 他们重新建立了与那个人的联结，而这与创伤无关。

sentences.en: But absolutely, as you've said, Marianne, I haven't had anyone leave therapy that's had a loss that is going, well, I feel nothing about that now.
sentences.zh: 但绝对就像你所说的，玛丽安，我没有让任何经历过丧亲之痛的客户在离开治疗时会说：“嗯，我现在对那件事毫无感觉了。”

sentences.en: But what they do get is a different relationship to the lost one back.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实找回了与逝者的一种不同的关系。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And you begin to be able to assimilate it better into your life rather than it just jutting out like this sudden stone wall.
sentences.zh: 你开始能够更好地将它融入你的生活，而不是让它像一堵突然出现的大石墙那样突兀地杵在那里。

sentences.en: And, yeah, like it's sometimes with grief, like you said, it can be so sudden.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，就像你说的，有时悲伤会非常突然。

sentences.en: And there can also be bits where caregivers and loved ones are having to be involved in that.
sentences.zh: 而且还可能伴随着照顾者和亲人不得不参与其中的片段。

sentences.en: So perhaps they're having to do CPR.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他们不得不进行心肺复苏（CPR）。

sentences.en: Perhaps they're having to manage the situation, you know, over the phone.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不得不通过电话来处理当时的情况。

sentences.en: And all of that can be an added trauma that is just not lying flat.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都可能成为一种额外的创伤，而这些创伤根本没有平复。

sentences.en: No, sure.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, you know, when you were talking to us about how trauma can mean that you disengage from your life and stop doing all the things that you love,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当你跟我们谈到创伤如何意味着你会脱离生活、停止做所有你热爱的事情时，

sentences.en: I just felt so proud to do what we do, Alex, because I just thought, God, we get to be in a position where we see people just come back to themselves.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常自豪，能做我们现在所做的事情，亚历克斯，因为我只是觉得，天哪，我们有机会看到人们重新找回自我。

sentences.en: And they suddenly like, God, I really missed myself or other people start to notice that with them, like, oh, you smile or you did this or you just seemed very different.
sentences.zh: 他们突然觉得：“天哪，我真的很想念过去的自己。”或者其他人开始注意到他们身上的变化，比如，“哦，你笑了”或者“你做了这个”或者“你看起来真的很不一样”。

sentences.en: And it's so powerful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太有力量了，对吧？

sentences.en: Tell us about how EMDR can help us to help people to reconnect with their lives again.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲EMDR如何帮助我们引导人们重新与他们的生活建立联结。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, I think, you know, like I was saying, sometimes people are they haven't meant to cut off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，你知道的，就像我刚才说的，有时候人们并不是故意要切断联系。

sentences.en: They're just that, you know, like the head has had to carry on life doing life, you know, but the feelings aren't allowed to be around because they're too overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 他们只是，你知道的，就像大脑不得不继续过日子、生活，你知道的，但是不允许情绪出现，因为情绪太压抑了。

sentences.en: And so what EMDR will do is if we can bring if we can bring up like you just gave me an example of what we would call a target in EMDR,
sentences.zh: 所以EMDR的作用是，如果我们能把……如果我们能把你在EMDR中称之为“目标”的东西调动起来——就像你刚才举的那个例子一样，

sentences.en: when that moment where your dad had a stumble and for you that just wasn't settling, we would call that a target in EMDr.
sentences.zh: 你父亲踉跄的那一刻，对你来说就是无法释怀，在EMDR中我们称之为目标。

sentences.en: I call them hot spots with people typically because within, you know, often it's a chapter in someone's life, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我通常称它们为“热点”，因为在很多情况下，它往往是人生活中的一个章节，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not that one off event that happened in a split second and was done.
sentences.zh: 它不是那种在电光石火间发生并结束的单一事件。

sentences.en: And, you know, often we're working with people on things that have gone on for hours, weeks, months, years sometimes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们经常与人们一起处理那些持续了几个小时、几周、几个月甚至有时几年的事情。

sentences.en: And so we look in the story for what these particular hot moments, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在故事中寻找这些特定的高光时刻，如果你愿意这么叫的话。

sentences.en: And in EMDR, we would prime that moment.
sentences.zh: 在EMDR中，我们会对那个时刻进行预处理。

sentences.en: So we get those fragments out the cupboard.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把那些碎片从储藏柜里拿出来。

sentences.en: We would have created the safe relationship and the safe space.
sentences.zh: 我们会建立安全的关系和安全的空间。

sentences.en: And then we would be allowing the brain time to decompress, I guess, like defrag that difficult moment until it's not as overwhelming anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会给大脑时间去减压，我想就像对那个困难的时刻进行碎片整理一样，直到它不再那么令人难以承受。

sentences.en: And then the person will.
sentences.zh: 然后这个人就会……

sentences.en: Well, let me say another way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，换一种说法。

sentences.en: I had one client many years, many years ago who summed up, I think, what EMDR does really, really nicely.
sentences.zh: 多年前，我曾有一个客户，她对EMDR的作用做了一个非常非常精彩的总结。

sentences.en: And I use this example on my training.
sentences.zh: 我在我的培训中经常使用这个例子。

sentences.en: So she had actually had a car crash and she had gone to see a therapist for CBT.
sentences.zh: 她其实遭遇过车祸，并曾去看过认知行为疗法（CBT）治疗师。

sentences.en: That was what she was, you know, and rightly so.
sentences.zh: 那是她当时所接受的，你知道的，而且理应如此。

sentences.en: Trauma focused CBT was completely appropriate according to the NICE guidelines.
sentences.zh: 根据NICE指南，聚焦创伤的CBT是完全合适的。

sentences.en: But it hadn't worked.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有起作用。

sentences.en: It hadn't taken the edge off.
sentences.zh: 它并没有减轻那种痛苦的边缘。

sentences.en: And then she came to see me for EMDr.
sentences.zh: 然后她来找我做EMDR。

sentences.en: And when we'd done the EMDR and it had been really successful, I asked her, what was different?
sentences.zh: 当我们做完EMDR并且非常成功后，我问她：有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: You've had both.
sentences.zh: 这两种疗法你都体验过了。

sentences.en: And she said, you know, I feel like CBT was going, if you can think differently about this, you will feel differently about it.
sentences.zh: 她说：“你知道，我觉得CBT就像是在说，如果你能对这件事有不同的想法，你对它的感觉就会不同。”

sentences.en: She said, but I couldn't do that because when the feelings showed up, they were so strong that I couldn't think rationally.
sentences.zh: 她说：“但我做不到，因为当情绪涌现时，它们是如此强烈，以至于我根本无法理性思考。”

sentences.en: And what we did in the EMDR is we made space for the feelings and we processed the feelings about what had happened.
sentences.zh: “而我们在EMDR中所做的是，我们为情绪腾出了空间，并处理了关于所发生事情的情绪。”

sentences.en: They dialed down.
sentences.zh: “情绪降温了。”

sentences.en: And then naturally, I thought differently about stuff.
sentences.zh: “然后自然而然地，我对事情有了不同的看法。”

sentences.en: And I think that's some way of answering your question.
sentences.zh: 我想这算是在某种程度上回答了你的问题。

sentences.en: How do people reconnect with life?
sentences.zh: 人们是如何重新与生活建立联结的？

sentences.en: Because when people have got, often with traumatic events, people will have a number of negative beliefs, either about themselves, other people, the world.
sentences.zh: 因为当人们经历过创伤事件时，往往会产生许多负面的信念，无论是关于他们自己、其他人还是这个世界。

sentences.en: That might be, I'm a failure.
sentences.zh: 那可能是：我是一个失败者。

sentences.en: I get things wrong.
sentences.zh: 我总是把事情搞砸。

sentences.en: I mess up or I'm in danger or I'm not in control.
sentences.zh: 我把事情弄得一团糟，或者我处于危险之中，或者我无法掌控。

sentences.en: Other people are not trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 其他人是不值得信任的。

sentences.en: The world isn't safe.
sentences.zh: 这个世界是不安全的。

sentences.en: And so people learn to shut down and cut off because that is self-preservation.
sentences.zh: 所以人们学会了自我关闭和切断联系，因为这是自我保护。

sentences.en: But actually, when these beliefs shift in therapy, which they do, when the high distress comes down, the thinking brain will come back online more naturally.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当这些信念在治疗中发生转变时——它们确实会发生转变——当高度的痛苦消退时，思考的大脑就会更加自然地重新上线。

sentences.en: And then people can re-engage with life because not only are they not disconnected from it anymore because their feelings about stuff do start to come back.
sentences.zh: 然后人们就可以重新投入到生活中，因为他们不仅不再与生活断连，因为他们对事物的感受开始回归了。

sentences.en: But in a healthy way, like we said with the grief, when their beliefs shift into much healthier sets of beliefs, like I'm okay, it's over, I'm good enough.
sentences.zh: 而且是以一种健康的方式，就像我们讨论悲伤时所说的那样，当他们的信念转变成更加健康的信念时，比如：我很好，已经结束了，我足够好了。

sentences.en: Other people are, you know, some people are trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 其他人是……你知道的，有些人是值得信任的。

sentences.en: The world is safe enough.
sentences.zh: 这个世界足够安全。

sentences.en: Then they can venture into life again, you know, feeling more robuSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就可以再次闯荡生活，你知道的，感觉更加强韧。

sentences.en: And that's what helps people reconnect with people, places, activities that they used to enjoy.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点帮助人们重新与人、与地点、与他们曾经喜欢活动的建立联结。

sentences.en: It really does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it can be such a visceral experience to carry trauma.
sentences.zh: 背负创伤可以是一种非常触及腹心的体验。

sentences.en: I'm reminded of a case I worked with.
sentences.zh: 我想起我处理过的一个案例。

sentences.en: And whilst EMDR breakthroughs don't all happen at the same time in session one, we often will get, you know, what John Burnham in systemic therapy refers to as magic moments,
sentences.zh: 虽然EMDR的突破并不都在第一节课同时发生，但我们通常会得到，你知道的，正如约翰·伯纳姆在系统疗法中所指出的那种“神奇时刻”，

sentences.en: where you can literally just have this real transformational moment.
sentences.zh: 在那里你真的可以拥有这种真正的转化时刻。

sentences.en: And I had this experience in EMDR with a client where at the end of the session, they said, well,
sentences.zh: 我之前在对一位来访者进行EMDR治疗时有过这样一段经历：在咨询结束时，他们说，嗯，

sentences.en: it feels like I've put down these heavy shopping bags that I've been carrying for almost 10 years that I didn't realize I was carrying.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我放下了这些沉重的购物袋，这些袋子我已经背了快十年了，而我以前甚至都没意识到自己一直在扛着它们。

sentences.en: And then today in this room is the first time I've realized what a weight that has been and what a relief it is to not have to carry that anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后今天在这间屋子里，我第一次意识到这曾经是多么沉重的一个负担，而不再背着它们又是多么地如释重负。

sentences.en: And then was able to really clearly say, well, now when I look back at that, that does feel like it's been getting on for 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 接着，他们能够非常清晰地表达：嗯，现在当我回想起过去时，那感觉确实像是快十年前的事了。

sentences.en: Was when I walked in here this morning, that felt like it was now, like I couldn't get that time, that time distinction, that filing cabinet label that we often think about.
sentences.zh: 而今天早上我走进来的时候，那感觉就像是发生在现在一样，我无法把握那种时间感，无法做出那种时间上的区分，也就是我们常说的那个档案柜标签。

sentences.en: I just couldn't get it.
sentences.zh: 我就是无法理清这种感觉。

sentences.en: It was so loose and fluid.
sentences.zh: 它是那么的模糊和流动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So people will say, you know, it feels like now, like when it shows up, when the cupboard flings open, it's literally happening again.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，你知道的，这感觉就像是发生在当下，每当它浮现、每当碗橱的门猛然敞开时，就好像这一切真的再次发生了。

sentences.en: And because of that, send off the person's threat system, their alarm system in their body will go again.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，这会触发个人的威胁系统，他们体内的警报系统会再次启动。

sentences.en: So it makes them feel like it's literally happening again.
sentences.zh: 所以这让他们觉得事情真的是在当下重新上演了一遍。

sentences.en: And people feel like they're going mad because they'll say, well, I know it's over, but I don't feel like that.
sentences.zh: 人们会觉得自己快要疯了，因为他们会说：“嗯，我知道已经结束了，但我感觉不到。”

sentences.en: And that's the difference, I think, with EMDR is we call it this head heart lag, if you like,
sentences.zh: 我认为，这正是EMDR的不同之处，我们称之为“头脑与内心的时滞”，如果你愿意这么叫的话，

sentences.en: or this head heart distinction where people might have done a lot of talking therapy and go, well, yeah, logically, I know it wasn't my fault or I know I'm safe.
sentences.zh: 或者叫头脑与内心的分歧——人们可能做过很多谈话疗法，然后会说：“嗯，对啊，从理性上讲，我知道这不是我的错，或者我知道我是安全的。”

sentences.en: But it doesn't feel like that.
sentences.zh: 但感觉上却并非如此。

sentences.en: But what we see in EMDR is when the high distress is dialed down, when the shopping bags get put down and the thinking brain can come online, the head can come online,
sentences.zh: 但在EMDR中我们看到的是，当高度的痛苦情绪降下来、当购物袋被放下、理性的思维能够上线、头脑能够恢复运作时，

sentences.en: we get a marrying up of the two.
sentences.zh: 这两者便开始走向融合。

sentences.en: So the cupboard is no longer flinging open.
sentences.zh: 因此，碗橱不会再猛然敞开了。

sentences.en: Actually, the cupboard's now been, I say to clients, it's like, we're going to empty the cupboard safely, carefully, bit by bit.
sentences.zh: 事实上，碗橱现在已经被——我会对来访者说，这就像是：我们要安全、仔细地把碗橱清空，一点一点地来。

sentences.en: We're going to sort out this stuff and put it somewhere else so the door isn't, you know, stuffing a load of stuff away anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们要把这些东西分类整理好，放到别的地方去，这样门就不会再——你知道的，不会再往里面塞满各种东西了。

sentences.en: It's not, they're not vulnerable to the cupboard door flinging open anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再是这样了，他们不再那么容易受到碗橱门猛然敞开的困扰了。

sentences.en: And as you say, Marianne, you know, it's not always like a real quick win in EMDr.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，玛丽安，你知道的，在EMDR中并不总能那么快就取得立竿见影的成果。

sentences.en: For some clients, it really is.
sentences.zh: 对某些来访者来说，确实如此。

sentences.en: For other clients, it's much more of an up and down process in therapy, especially the longer term, more chronically traumatized someone is, the harder it is.
sentences.zh: 而对另一些来访者而言，在治疗中这是一个更多起伏的过程，尤其是那些经历更久、创伤更慢性的人，过程就会越艰难。

sentences.en: But it will, it can get there for sure.
sentences.zh: 但它肯定会达到那个效果，一定能做到。

sentences.en: But yeah, you're, you know, you talked about how visceral and that's the head heart, that's the head body distinction, right?
sentences.zh: 不过是的，你刚才谈到了那种深切的身体感受，这就是头脑与心、头脑与身体的区别，对吧？

sentences.en: Because people literally feel stuff in EMDR, don't they?
sentences.zh: 因为人们在EMDR中真的能真切地感受到各种感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: And sometimes people don't like that because the feelings are horrible and they've done a really good job of cutting off from them.
sentences.zh: 有时人们并不喜欢这样，因为这些感觉太可怕了，而他们过去在切断与这些感受的联系方面做得“非常好”。

sentences.en: But if we can bring the feelings into the space safely and process them and they can get filed away differently in the brain with that date stamp of it's over, that was then,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能安全地把这些感受带入空间并进行加工，它们就能在头脑中以不同的方式被归档，并贴上“已经结束、那是过去”的日期戳，

sentences.en: not it's now.
sentences.zh: 而不是“现在正在发生”。

sentences.en: People really, really benefit from that.
sentences.zh: 人们真的、真的会从中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: Had a veteran come to see me a few years back who had a very bad stammer when I met him to the point where I couldn't really understand a lot of what he was saying,
sentences.zh: 几年前，曾有一位退伍老兵来找我求助，我见到他时，他有非常严重的口吃，以至于我很难听懂他说的很多话，

sentences.en: which EMDR was great for because you don't need to talk a lot in EMDR, but I really, that was one of these moments where he was a little bit stuck on something.
sentences.zh: 这使得EMDR非常适用，因为在EMDR中你不需要说太多话，但真的，有这么一个时刻，他在某个地方稍微卡住了。

sentences.en: And I said something like, do you need to keep doing that now you're safe in the UK?
sentences.zh: 我大概说了这样一句话：“既然你现在在英国已经安全了，你还需要继续这样做吗？”

sentences.en: And he went, no.
sentences.zh: 他回答说：“不需要。”

sentences.en: And I said, okay, go with that.
sentences.zh: 我说：“好的，顺着这个感觉走。”

sentences.en: And we added some more BLS.
sentences.zh: 于是我们增加了一些双侧刺激（BLS）。

sentences.en: And he went, oh, something left my body and his stammer had gone.
sentences.zh: 接着他说：“哦，有什么东西从我身体里离开了。”他的口吃居然就这样消失了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's just weird and amazing all in one go.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道的，这既诡异又神奇，两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: But that talks to that, how visceral stuff is.
sentences.zh: 但这说明了那种身体感受是多么的直观和深刻。

sentences.en: And it's implicit.
sentences.zh: 而且它是内隐的。

sentences.en: A lot of stuff is implicit for people.
sentences.zh: 对人们来说，很多东西都是内隐的。

sentences.en: The brain hasn't had a chance to put the story on and make really good sense of it.
sentences.zh: 大脑甚至还没有机会把这个故事串联起来并赋予它真正合理的解释。

sentences.en: And if you think back to, you know, for some clients we're working with when they were really little and they won't have a coherent narrative of that event,
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下，你知道的，对于我们接待的一些来访者来说，当他们还很小的时候，他们对那段经历根本没有连贯的叙述，

sentences.en: but the body is holding the shopping bags.
sentences.zh: 但他们的身体却一直提着那些购物袋。

sentences.en: Yeah, what a really powerful moment and what a privilege to be there for these really authentic, vulnerable human moments.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个多么强有力的时刻，能够见证这些极其真实、脆弱的人类情感时刻又是何等的荣幸。

sentences.en: And obviously this can be incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这可能会极其艰难。

sentences.en: You know, you and I have both been in sessions with people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你我都曾和来访者一同经历过这样的咨询。

sentences.en: You and I have both probably been clients where we've just been like a snotty mess when we're having EMDr.
sentences.zh: 你我都可能当过这样的来访者：在做EMDR时哭得鼻涕眼泪一大把，狼狈不堪。

sentences.en: Like it can be really, really evocative.
sentences.zh: 这确实可能带来非常强烈的情感触动。

sentences.en: But what I would say and what I know you would want to make clear is this is not uncontainable.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，而且我也知道你会希望澄清这一点：这是完全可以承受和控制的。

sentences.en: This is not unmanageable.
sentences.zh: 这并非无法管理。

sentences.en: You know, we would always make sure that a client was safe and could be well resourced to be able to be stable so that they weren't left managing this after a session.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们总是会确保来访者是安全的，并为他们提供充足的资源支持，让他们能够保持稳定，这样他们在咨询结束后就不会独自去面对这些情绪的余波。

sentences.en: EMDR, I'm always really sad and disappointed when I get people coming to me saying I had EMDr.
sentences.zh: 对于EMDR，每当听到有人来找我并说“我做过EMDR，那体验简直糟透了，真的带来了二次创伤，我再也不想经历了”，我都感到非常难过和失望。

sentences.en: It was absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 那体验简直糟透了。

sentences.en: It was really re-traumatizing.
sentences.zh: 真的带来了二次创伤。

sentences.en: I never want that again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不想经历了。

sentences.en: And often when I say, could you tell me a bit about that?
sentences.zh: 通常当我问：“你能跟我多讲讲那次经历吗？”

sentences.en: Like what, like how quickly did you get in processing it?
sentences.zh: 比如“你们当时是以多快的速度进入加工环节的？”

sentences.en: And often I hear it straight away.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到的回答是：一上来就开始了。

sentences.en: We were processing straight away.
sentences.zh: 我们一上来就在进行加工。

sentences.en: And that I know there are definitely therapists that do that.
sentences.zh: 我知道确实有些治疗师是这么做的。

sentences.en: And certainly there's a big, you know, group of people in the Netherlands who work in an inpatient service who do process with people really quickly.
sentences.zh: 当然，荷兰有一大批在住院部服务的专业人员，他们确实会非常快地与来访者一起进行创伤加工。

sentences.en: But it's within the containment and safety of an inpatient service.
sentences.zh: 但那是在住院部所具备的包容与安全的框架内进行的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think what some EMDR therapists will who have trained in it or not trained in it, which is the bigger issue.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，有些EMDR治疗师——无论是接受过正规培训的还是没受过培训的（这才是更大的问题）。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because anyone can go and do a training that isn't regulated.
sentences.zh: 因为任何人都可以去参加一个不受监管的培训。

sentences.en: And this is where the problems can stem from.
sentences.zh: 而问题往往正是由此产生的。

sentences.en: But, yeah, some people think it's a technique.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，有些人认为这只是一种技术。

sentences.en: Like if I just do this to somebody, that's going to magically make their trauma process.
sentences.zh: 仿佛只要我对某人做了这个动作，就能像变魔术一样让他们大脑中的创伤得到加工。

sentences.en: But actually, I'm a big, big advocate.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我非常、非常主张——

sentences.en: And I'm sure, you know, this is what Francine Shapiro was teaching is you don't just sit in front of somebody and say, well,
sentences.zh: 我确信，你知道的，这也是法兰妮·夏琵罗（Francine Shapiro）一直所教导的：你不能只是坐在一个人面前然后说：“好吧，去想那件事”，然后就开始任由他们心中的碗橱猛然敞开。

sentences.en: think of that and then start let the cupboard in the mind fling open.
sentences.zh: 思考那件事，然后开始让头脑里的碗橱猛然敞开。

sentences.en: You and I know and all my supervisees work to actually you spend a good amount of time building a strong relationship with that person.
sentences.zh: 你我都清楚，我所有的督导对象也都在这样做：实际上，你需要花相当长的时间与那个人建立牢固的关系。

sentences.en: And looking at their risk history, checking what they can and can't manage processing.
sentences.zh: 还要评估他们的风险历史，核实他们能够或不能够承受什么程度的加工。

sentences.en: And I always say to my clients, you didn't have control at the time of the trauma.
sentences.zh: 我总是对我的来访者说：“在创伤发生时，你没有掌控权。”

sentences.en: I want you to have control in the room with me.
sentences.zh: “但我希望你在我这间咨询室里拥有掌控权。”

sentences.en: You need to have a sense of being in the driving seat.
sentences.zh: “你需要有那种掌握方向盘的感觉。”

sentences.en: I'm alongside you.
sentences.zh: “我陪在你身旁。”

sentences.en: I'm helping you navigate.
sentences.zh: “我在协助你前行。”

sentences.en: But only you can decide how much you do or don't do and what you process.
sentences.zh: “但只有你才能决定自己要做多少、不做多少，以及你要加工什么。”

sentences.en: So I have some clients say, coming for the car crash, I absolutely am not touching my childhood trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以有些来访者会说：“我是为了车祸来的，我绝对不要触碰我的童年创伤。”

sentences.en: And I'm like, fine, you know, we have to be respectful.
sentences.zh: 而我会说：“好的，没问题。”你知道的，我们必须尊重来访者。

sentences.en: But sometimes clients don't get that message.
sentences.zh: 但有时候来访者并没有接收到这个信息。

sentences.en: It's like, just get on with it.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是：别管那么多，直接开始吧。

sentences.en: And we're going right back here to, you know, this stuff that happened to you when you were seven or eight.
sentences.zh: 我们要直接回到这里，回到那些你七八岁时发生在你身上的事情上。

sentences.en: And clients don't know that actually they should have more of a voice than that.
sentences.zh: 而来访者并不知道，实际上他们本该拥有更多的话语权。

sentences.en: So, no, EMDR should never be.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，EMDR绝不应该是这样的。

sentences.en: It's not reliving this very much a mindfulness component with EMDR that should absolutely be present in every session, where we call it dual awareness.
sentences.zh: 这并不是在重新体验过去，在EMDR中有一个非常重要的正念成分，它绝对应该存在于每一次咨询中，我们称之为“双重觉察”。

sentences.en: So whilst you're noticing this difficult thing here, you know, we've got some stuff out the cupboard.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你在觉察眼前这个困难的事情时，你知道的，我们把碗橱里的一些东西拿了出来。

sentences.en: You're not reliving it.
sentences.zh: 你并不是在重新经历它。

sentences.en: Actually, we need you to have very much a sense of safety in the here and now in the therapy space, whether that's online or whether that's physically in a room with somebody.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们需要你在此时此地的治疗空间里拥有强烈的安全感，无论这是在线上进行，还是在现实的咨询室里与某人面对面。

sentences.en: We're saying to them from the safety of the now, I want you to just observe, just notice that thing that happened back then.
sentences.zh: 我们在以此时此地的安全感为基础，对他们说：我希望你去观察、去留意过去发生的那件事。

sentences.en: They're not meant to be reliving it.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是要去重新经历它。

sentences.en: Obviously, people can get a bit flooded,
sentences.zh: 当然，人们有时可能会情绪泛滥，

sentences.en: but that's the therapist's role is to co-regulate that person in the space where we're not meant to sit silently and just say nothing and be completely neutral.
sentences.zh: 但治疗师的角色正是在这个空间里与该人进行共调节，我们绝不能只是默默坐着什么都不说，表现得完全中立。

sentences.en: We're not interfering with the processing, but we absolutely are holding the space non-verbally, verbally.
sentences.zh: 我们不会干扰加工过程，但我们绝对会通过非语言和语言的方式来承载这个空间。

sentences.en: You know, we're not talking to them the whole time, but they should be very aware of our presence.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们并不是一直在跟他们说话，但他们应该能非常清晰地感受到我们的存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really agree with you that this is safer in inexperienced kind of hands.
sentences.zh: 是的，我非常赞同你的看法，在经验不足的人手里，这确实存在风险。

sentences.en: And I didn't learn this until I was already a qualified psychologist and it felt like it was an additional tool in my toolkit.
sentences.zh: 我直到自己已经成为一名合格的心理学家时才学会这个，当时感觉这就像是我工具箱里的一个额外工具。

sentences.en: But I'm very glad it's not my only tool in my toolkit, because like you, I believe that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我非常高兴它不是我工具箱里唯一的工具，因为和 S 你们一样，我认为，你知道的——

sentences.en: all the other things I've learned along the way and had experience of with clients are so important.
sentences.zh: 我在这一路上学到的所有其他东西以及与来访者相处的经验都是如此重要。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I was going to say, you know, for accredited trainers, EMDR trainers in the UK, you know, we've all gone through pretty rigorous, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你知道的，对于英国的认证培训师、EMDR培训师来说，你知道的，我们都经历过相当严格的、你知道的——

sentences.en: things in order to demonstrate our competencies.
sentences.zh: 各种考核，以证明我们的能力。

sentences.en: And that's why there's an eligibility criteria to get on accredited trainings.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么想要参加认证培训必须满足一定的准入标准。

sentences.en: You already need to be a pretty well-established therapist because you need the foundational skills.
sentences.zh: 你本身就需要是一位相当成熟的治疗师，因为你需要具备基础技能。

sentences.en: If you don't have the skills to sit with someone in their distress and manage risk and co-regulate someone and know who to ring and what to do.
sentences.zh: 如果你连陪同一位痛苦中的来访者、管理风险、与来访者进行共调节，以及知道该打电话给谁、该做什么都不具备这些能力的话，

sentences.en: If someone is quite distressed or you don't know how to bring someone back into their window of tolerance, you shouldn't be doing EMDr.
sentences.zh: 如果某个来访者非常痛苦，或者你不知道如何将一个人拉回到他们的耐受窗口内，你就不应该去做EMDR。

sentences.en: That's why there's an eligibility criteria.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么会有准入标准。

sentences.en: And that's why I get frustrated when people set themselves up as trainers who have none of none of those skills and actively advertise.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么每当看到有人自己开设培训班、却完全不具备这些技能还大肆进行广告宣传时，我会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: We don't have an eligibility criteria.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何准入标准。

sentences.en: And I think what a shame for the public who won't know the difference, you know, because they don't know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这对公众来说太遗憾了，他们根本分不清区别，你知道的，因为他们不懂。

sentences.en: So someone advertises that they're an EMDR therapist, go and have EMDR, have a really, sometimes really bad experience and never,
sentences.zh: 所以有人打广告说自己是EMDR治疗师，然后公众去做了EMDR，有了一次非常糟糕、有时甚至是极差的体验，再也——

sentences.en: and they're more traumatised and never want to do it again.
sentences.zh: 结果受了更深的创伤，再也不想尝试了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are different levels of qualification and experience with EMDr.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，EMDR的资质和经验是分为不同等级的。

sentences.en: Can you take us through what they might look like, Alex?
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，你能给我们介绍一下这些不同的级别大概是怎样的吗？

sentences.en: Sure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然可以，没问题。

sentences.en: So to get on accredited training in the UK, as I said, you already have to meet an eligibility criteria.
sentences.zh: 所以在英国要参加认证培训，正如我所说，你首先必须满足准入标准。

sentences.en: And that, you know,
sentences.zh: 而这，你知道的——

sentences.en: I'm not going to tell you about all of them right here because they're on the EMDR Association UK's website and they're on my training website and all the other trainers' websites.
sentences.zh: 我不会在这里把所有标准都讲一遍，因为它们都在英国EMDR协会的网站上，在我的培训网站上，以及所有其他培训师的网站上都能找到。

sentences.en: But your first, so your first, different trainers do it slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 但你的第一步，也就是最初的阶段，不同的培训师做法会略有不同。

sentences.en: Some, like me, will have three parts.
sentences.zh: 有些人，比如我，会分成三个部分。

sentences.en: Some have what we call four parts.
sentences.zh: 有些人采用我们所谓的四个部分。

sentences.en: And that's essentially because they've split the supervision day into two halves to give people a little bit longer to get things under their belt.
sentences.zh: 这主要是因为他们把督导日拆成了两个半天，好给学员多一点时间来掌握所学内容。

sentences.en: And also a whole day of supervision is quite long for people, you know, so you can probably imagine.
sentences.zh: 而且整整一天的督导对大家来说也确实挺漫长的，你知道的，所以你可以想象一下。

sentences.en: So, but the material covered is, to all intents and purposes, the same.
sentences.zh: 因此，但实际上所涵盖的内容在所有意图和目的上都是一样的。

sentences.en: So all trainers will have to do 24 hours of teaching, 18 hours of practicals and 10 hours of supervision.
sentences.zh: 所以所有培训师都必须完成24小时的授课、18小时的实践操作以及10小时的督导。

sentences.en: So some people might do level one or part one.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人可能会学第一级或第一部分。

sentences.en: We call it part one, part two, part three and or part four, depending on which trainer they're going with.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为第一部分、第二部分、第三部分，或者第四部分，这取决于他们跟随哪位培训师学习。

sentences.en: That's called standard training.
sentences.zh: 这被称为标准培训。

sentences.en: And at that stage, you can call yourself a part one trained EMDR therapist or a part three trained EMDR therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你可以称自己为“第一部分培训合格的EMDR治疗师”或“第三部分培训合格的EMDR治疗师”。

sentences.en: Then that's not accredited.
sentences.zh: 但那还不是认证级别。

sentences.en: You're not, there's no assessment process for that.
sentences.zh: 你并没有——没有针对这个阶段的考核流程。

sentences.en: Obviously, you have to join in in all the activities on the trainings and you have to demonstrate a level of competency.
sentences.zh: 当然，你必须参加培训中的所有活动，并且必须展现出一定水平的能力。

sentences.en: But we're not assessing you on that because you're just literally learning.
sentences.zh: 但我们不会就此对你进行考核，因为你目前正处于纯粹的学习阶段。

sentences.en: It's like the learning to drive, but then the getting good at it comes with the supervision and the hours of having a go.
sentences.zh: 这就好比学开车，而真正变得熟练则需要通过后期的督导以及大量的实际练习来积累。

sentences.en: And like you said, we're, you know, learning through our mistakes sometimes, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们，你知道的，有时是通过犯错来学习的，不是吗？

sentences.en: And and some of the most important learning experiences come through that.
sentences.zh: 而一些最重要的学习经历正是由此而来的。

sentences.en: But so the next level up from that, which is called accredited, is practitioner, which you can apply for just around about one year after you finish your part three.
sentences.zh: 所以，比这更高的下一个级别被称为“认证执业医师”（Accredited Practitioner），你可以在完成第三部分后的大约一年左右申请。

sentences.en: So you have to be fully standard trained in order to then go towards practitioner.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须接受过完整的标准培训，才能进而申请执业认证。

sentences.en: And that is very much more of a rigorous assessment process where you need to see a minimum of 25 clients that you've processed with.
sentences.zh: 这是一个要求更加严格的评估过程，你需要提交至少25个你亲自做过创伤加工的来访者案例。

sentences.en: You need to have had another 10 hours minimum of supervision on top of what you had on your training.
sentences.zh: 除了培训期间的要求外，你还需要额外进行至少10小时的督导。

sentences.en: It's a very competency based.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常注重能力的考核过程。

sentences.en: So it's not even a numbers game.
sentences.zh: 所以这甚至不是一个单纯拼数量的游戏。

sentences.en: You know, some people will say, well, I must be nearly there now because I've done, you know, they might contact me via my website and say, oh,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有些人会说：“嗯，我肯定快达到了，因为我已经做了——”他们可能会通过我的网站联系我并说：“哦，

sentences.en: could you see me through to practitioner?
sentences.zh: 你能带我完成执业认证的流程吗？

sentences.en: Because I've done 23 clients.
sentences.zh: 因为我已经做了23个来访者了。”

sentences.en: I'm nearly there.
sentences.zh: 我快完成了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, well, I actually need to be confident that you know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 然后我就觉得，实际上我得确信你知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: So that's going to probably be another year, if I'm honest with me, before I feel like that we're there because you have to see video footage and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以说实话，在我感觉我们真的达成目标之前，可能还得再花一年时间，因为你必须查看视频录像之类的所有东西。

sentences.en: So you can hear it's quite an extra bit of work on compared to like your standard training, but it does demonstrate good clinical competency.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以听到，与标准培训相比，这确实需要付出额外的工作，但这确实证明了良好的临床能力。

sentences.en: If you get there, you can go on the EMDR Association map and be searchable.
sentences.zh: 如果你达到了这个水平，你就可以登上EMDR协会的地图并被搜索到。

sentences.en: And then, you know, that's kind of your seal of approval.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，你知道，这就好比是你的批准印章。

sentences.en: If you've made it to the map, you've demonstrated your competency at practitioner level.
sentences.zh: 如果你成功登上了地图，就说明你已经证明了自己作为从业者的能力。

sentences.en: And then from there, if people want to, they can then go on to become a consultant.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，如果人们愿意，他们可以继续成为顾问。

sentences.en: So you're in essentially a what we call consultant in training period for a minimum of three years after practitioner level.
sentences.zh: 所以，在达到从业者水平之后，你基本上要经历一个我们称之为培训顾问的时期，至少持续三年。

sentences.en: Some people take longer.
sentences.zh: 有些人需要更长时间。

sentences.en: Some people are like really, you know, get through it really quickly and really adapted it.
sentences.zh: 有些人则会真的，你知道，非常快地通过并真正掌握了它。

sentences.en: But it's another three years minimum from practitioner level.
sentences.zh: 但从从业者水平算起，至少还要再过三年。

sentences.en: And for that, it's much more about your supervision of other people.
sentences.zh: 为此，这更多地关乎你对其他人的督导。

sentences.en: So really understanding that standard protocol and many other treatment plans inside, out, back to front and being able to support someone else to learn how to do EMDr.
sentences.zh: 所以要真正深刻理解那个标准协议以及许多其他治疗方案，从里到外、融会贯通，并能够支持其他人学习如何做EMDR。

sentences.en: But they're not teaching people EMDr. That's a trainer that would do that.
sentences.zh: 但他们不是在教人们EMDR。那是培训师做的事。

sentences.en: And then the next level up from there is facilitator where people might work towards facilitating trainings.
sentences.zh: 在那之上的一级是督导，人们可能会朝着协助培训的方向努力。

sentences.en: And again, that's several years on from there.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是在此基础上的好几年之后。

sentences.en: And then someone might become a trainer and then they might become a senior trainer.
sentences.zh: 然后某人可能会成为培训师，接着他们可能会成为高级培训师。

sentences.en: So there's like multiple sort of gateways, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，这里有多种类似的门槛。

sentences.en: But practitioners, your first level where it's like, right, you've demonstrated this competency and you're on the map.
sentences.zh: 但从业者是你的第一个级别，就像是，没错，你已经证明了这种能力并且上了地图。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Alex.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: And I know that having been your supervisee for quite a few years now, I know that you have, you know, you were doing your facilitating.
sentences.zh: 我知道，作为你多年的被督导者，我知道你一直在做督导工作。

sentences.en: And then you are now a trainer as well.
sentences.zh: 然后你现在也是一名培训师了。

sentences.en: And you've got your own training company.
sentences.zh: 而且你还有你自己的培训公司。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit about what you offer, Alex?
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯，能跟我们简单介绍一下你提供的内容吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we've got two businesses, essentially.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上有两项业务。

sentences.en: The business that I see you in is my what I call my therapy and supervision business.
sentences.zh: 我与你见面的这项业务是我所谓的治疗与督导业务。

sentences.en: So that's where I see my own clinical caseload, because as a no matter how high up you are in EMDR,
sentences.zh: 这就是我接待自己临床案例的地方，因为无论你在EMDR领域达到多高的地位，

sentences.en: you obviously still need to keep your feet on the ground and do the work yourself.
sentences.zh: 你显然仍然需要脚踏实地，自己动手做临床工作。

sentences.en: So we as trainers, facilitators, we always still have a therapy caseload.
sentences.zh: 所以我们作为培训师和督导，总是仍然会有治疗案例。

sentences.en: So my one side of the business is therapy where I see clients.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的业务的一方面是接待来访者的治疗。

sentences.en: They often come through my website or and then I do a lot of supervision online for clinicians like you in private practice.
sentences.zh: 他们通常通过我的网站来找我，或者我为像你这样在私人执业中的临床医生在线做大量的督导。

sentences.en: Or I do a huge amount of NHS supervision, again, mostly online.
sentences.zh: 或者我做大量的NHS（国民保健制度）督导，同样，主要也是在线上。

sentences.en: So that's the one strand of the business.
sentences.zh: 所以这是业务的一个方面。

sentences.en: And then more recently, we set up a training business.
sentences.zh: 然后更近一点，我们建立了一家培训业务。

sentences.en: So I qualified late 2024.
sentences.zh: 我在2024年底获得了资格。

sentences.en: But in the time it took us to get everything up and running, we ran our first training in April 2025.
sentences.zh: 但在我们筹备一切并使其正常运转期间，我们在2025年4月举办了第一次培训。

sentences.en: And we've run a few now.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经办了好几期了。

sentences.en: So we're based in South Devon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的基地在南德文郡。

sentences.en: We only currently offer in-person training because it's very experiential.
sentences.zh: 我们目前只提供线下培训，因为这非常注重体验。

sentences.en: And actually, I feel like for me, where I'm at with training at the minute,
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，我觉得对我而言，就我目前在培训方面的状态而言，

sentences.en: I want to have eyes on people in the room and be able to read the room and see how people are understanding what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我希望能够关注房间里的人，能够观察全场，看大家是如何理解我所说的话的。

sentences.en: But also for the practical side of things,
sentences.zh: 但对于实际操作方面，

sentences.en: I feel like you genuinely learn it much better when you're actually physically sat with someone having a go and you've got someone overseeing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当你真正身体力行地和某人坐在一起尝试，并且有旁人在旁边监督时，你确实能学得好得多。

sentences.en: And I just think whilst learning EMDR online is great, and I'm not saying I wouldn't move towards that at some point,
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，虽然在线学习EMDR很好，而且我并不是说在某个时候我不会朝着那个方向发展，

sentences.en: there's something about being in breakout rooms and not being visible all the time that stuff can get missed and lost a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但身处分组讨论室里却并不总是露面，这种情况下有些东西是会漏掉和迷失一点的。

sentences.en: And certainly when I've supervised people who trained purely online, when it comes to doing it in person with somebody, they're like, oh, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 而且毫无疑问，当我督导那些纯粹在线培训的人时，当涉及到与某人进行线下实操时，他们会说，哦，我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm not really sure about sitting with someone and doing that.
sentences.zh: 我真不确定怎么和别人坐在一起做那个。

sentences.en: So we offer the training.
sentences.zh: 所以我们提供培训。

sentences.en: Like I said, we're in the South WeSt.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我们在西南部。

sentences.en: So we physically have venues in Bristol and Torquay.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在布里斯托尔和托基都有实体场地。

sentences.en: But we do run in-house trainings.
sentences.zh: 但我们也确实举办内部培训。

sentences.en: We've run some for Cornwall.
sentences.zh: 我们为康沃尔郡办过一些。

sentences.en: We've run some for Avon and Wiltshire.
sentences.zh: 我们为埃文和威尔特郡办过一些。

sentences.en: And we're open to kind of going around the country and doing stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们也愿意去全国各地做一些事情。

sentences.en: But, yeah, that's what we do, really.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，这就是我们的工作，真的。

sentences.en: We're moving more towards being 50-50 therapy supervision and then the other side of the business being training.
sentences.zh: 我们正朝着50对50的方向发展，一半是治疗督导，业务的另一半则是培训。

sentences.en: Training.
sentences.zh: 培训。

sentences.en: Oh, we don't work with children.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们不接待儿童。

sentences.en: That's probably worth saying.
sentences.zh: 这可能值得提一下。

sentences.en: So I'm a standard trainer.
sentences.zh: 所以我是标准培训师。

sentences.en: So I don't have, even in my clinical psychology career, I think I did one child placement.
sentences.zh: 因此我没有，甚至在我的临床心理学职业生涯中，我想我只做过一次儿童实习。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't my thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那不是我的菜。

sentences.en: And so I've never, I did a little bit of child work because I did child training in EMDR and I did, I dipped my toe in.
sentences.zh: 所以我从来没有，我做过一点儿童工作，因为我在EMDR中做过儿童培训，我也浅尝辄止过。

sentences.en: But actually, I think, honestly, from my perspective, I think you need to have the core skills, like we were saying,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，老实说，从我的角度来看，我认为你需要拥有核心技能，就像我们刚才说的，

sentences.en: in working with children and families if you're going to offer EMDR to children.
sentences.zh: 如果你要为儿童提供EMDR治疗，你就需要在与儿童和家庭合作方面具备核心技能。

sentences.en: So, but what we have done is collaborate with a lady called Alice Vine, who is a child and adolescent trainer.
sentences.zh: 所以，但我们做的是与一位名叫爱丽丝·维恩的女士合作，她是一位儿童和青少年培训师。

sentences.en: But she's based up in Lincoln.
sentences.zh: 但她的基地在林肯。

sentences.en: But she's collaborating with us to bring EMDR child training to the southwest because there aren't any currently down here.
sentences.zh: 不过她正在与我们合作，将EMDR儿童培训带到西南部，因为这里目前还没有。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And I was just going to say, I'm aware that someone that we both met at one of my in-person psychology events, she is not based down in the southwest,
sentences.zh: 我正想说，我知道我们俩在我的一次线下心理学活动上遇到过一个人，她的基地不在西南部，

sentences.en: but treated it as an opportunity to have a few days on holiday in a hotel.
sentences.zh: 但她把这当成了一个在酒店度几天假的机会。

sentences.en: And so joined you from the Midlands.
sentences.zh: 所以她从米德兰兹赶来加入了你们。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you're willing to travel.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你愿意旅行的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the Bristol one's actually in a spa hotel.
sentences.zh: 布里斯托尔的那家其实是在一家水疗酒店里。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 真好。

sentences.en: You know, it's not to like.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很难让人不喜欢。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So people do use it as a getaway.
sentences.zh: 所以人们确实把它当成一个度假胜地。

sentences.en: Like they'll come down, have like the training is three days, but people might stay four or five.
sentences.zh: 比如他们会下来，培训是三天，但人们可能会呆四到五天。

sentences.en: And we have discounted rates at the hotels.
sentences.zh: 我们在酒店有折扣价。

sentences.en: And especially if you come in the sort of summer season and, you know, from sort of April onwards down here, it's really quite buzzing in Torquay.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你在夏季来，你知道，从四月份左右开始，这里的托基真的很热闹。

sentences.en: And there's been lots of regeneration in the area.
sentences.zh: 而且该地区有很多重建项目。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's quite being by the sea.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，靠海真的很不错。

sentences.en: People often come from, you know, places that, like you said, in the Midlands that are not, haven't got any sea near them for miles.
sentences.zh: 人们经常从，你知道的，像你说的米德兰兹那样方圆几英里内都没有海的地方来。

sentences.en: And they'll come down here and it's quite a refreshing break.
sentences.zh: 他们会来到这里，这是一个相当令人耳目一新的假期。

sentences.en: How nice.
sentences.zh: 多好啊。

sentences.en: I could talk to you all day, Alex.
sentences.zh: 我能跟你聊上一整天，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: Where can people learn more about you and your work?
sentences.zh: 人们可以在哪里了解更多关于你和你的工作？

sentences.en: What's your website?
sentences.zh: 你的网址是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So my website is www.doctorbutton-emdrtraining.co.uk.
sentences.zh: 我的网址是www.doctorbutton-emdrtraining.co.uk。

sentences.en: But if you Googled Alex Button EMDR training, it would show up in the searches as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在谷歌上搜索“Alex Button EMDR training”（亚历克斯·巴顿EMDR培训），它也会在搜索结果中显示出来。

sentences.en: And within that, we have a membership area that we've just generated in the last few months for our training delegates.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我们还有一个会员专区，这是我们在过去几个月里为我们的培训学员创建的。

sentences.en: But we open it up to EMDR therapists who've trained with another accredited trainer because lots of people were saying to us, it's a lot of information to take in in seven days.
sentences.zh: 但我们也对那些在其他认可培训师那里受过训的EMDR治疗师开放，因为很多人对我们说，在七天内要吸收的信息量太大了。

sentences.en: And I'd really would love to be able to watch it back or be able to come into like a joint kind of space to ask questions.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想能够回看，或者能够进入一个共同的空间来提问。

sentences.en: And so we generated the Refresh and Master membership area, which is also available via the website.
sentences.zh: 因此我们创建了“刷新与精通”会员专区，也可以通过网站访问。

sentences.en: So our training delegates get that for free for a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的培训学员可以免费获得一年的使用权。

sentences.en: And then, but then people who've trained with other people can also, as long as they can prove that they've trained properly,
sentences.zh: 然后，那些在其他人那里受过训的人也可以，只要他们能证明自己受过正规培训，

sentences.en: they can apply and have a monthly subscription to that.
sentences.zh: 他们就可以申请并按月订阅。

sentences.en: So that's got all the training videos, downloadable resources, links to lots of things, to WhatsApp,
sentences.zh: 那里有所有的培训视频、可下载的资源、各种链接、WhatsApp，

sentences.en: a WhatsApp group that's private and only questions are only answered by consultants that I know.
sentences.zh: 一个私密的WhatsApp群组，里面的问题只由我认识的督导来回答。

sentences.en: And two hours worth of drop in sessions a month where people can drop in.
sentences.zh: 以及每月两小时的答疑直通时间，人们可以随时加入。

sentences.en: It's not clinical supervision, but it's like a place to say, I got a bit stuck with this.
sentences.zh: 这不是临床督导，而是一个可以说“我在这一点上有点卡壳了”的地方。

sentences.en: Or can you tell me a bit more about EMDR for that?
sentences.zh: 或者“你能跟我多讲讲针对这种情况的EMDR吗？”

sentences.en: So we offer that in the membership area as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在会员专区也提供这些。

sentences.en: And that's available via the website.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过网站获取。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 太完美了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time, Alex.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: You really are like lovely at this and really good at what you do.
sentences.zh: 你真的很擅长这个，而且非常擅长你的工作。

sentences.en: So thank you for being a lovely gueSt.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你成为一个可爱的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Oh, no, thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: So lovely to have you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴有你做客。

sentences.en: Thanks, Alex.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: Wow, what a lovely chance to chat with Alex on camera.
sentences.zh: 哇，能在镜头前与亚历克斯聊天是多么美好的机会啊。

sentences.en: I am always just, I just feel so lucky to get to spend time with Alex.
sentences.zh: 我总是，我只是觉得自己太幸运了，能和亚历克斯一起度过时光。

sentences.en: She's so wise and being able to do so on camera, sharing it with you feels like a real treat as well.
sentences.zh: 她是如此睿智，能够在镜头前做到这一点并与你们分享，感觉也是一种真正的享受。

sentences.en: She just has a way of breaking things down that make everything seem to make sense.
sentences.zh: 她有一种把事情剖析清楚的能力，能让一切都变得合情合理。

sentences.en: I hope that you've got someone like that for you in your life.
sentences.zh: 我希望你的生活中也有这样一个人。

sentences.en: She's also really funny.
sentences.zh: 她也十分幽默。

sentences.en: And I love having her in my world for that reason too.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我也很喜欢让她的存在丰富我的世界。

sentences.en: We got together in person for the first time last summer at an in-person psychology networking event.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，我们在一个线下心理学社交活动中第一次见面。

sentences.en: And it was really special.
sentences.zh: 那真的很特别。

sentences.en: I love working with clinicians that are human and, you know, excellent at what they do.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢与有人情味、并且你知道的，在工作上极其优秀的临床医生合作。

sentences.en: And that's what I aim to bring you in psychology actually.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在《实际上是心理学》中力求带给你们的。

sentences.en: If you're not already following Dr. Alex Button on Instagram or LinkedIn, please do so.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有在Instagram或LinkedIn上关注亚历克斯·巴顿博士，请务必关注。

sentences.en: Her details are in the show notes or on screen.
sentences.zh: 她的详细信息在节目介绍中或屏幕上。

sentences.en: I certainly learn a lot from being in her world on LinkedIn where she's Dr. Alex Button.
sentences.zh: 我在LinkedIn上进入她的世界确实学到了很多，她在那里是亚历克斯·巴顿博士。

sentences.en: If you're an aspiring psychologist and you are striving to be a clinical psychologist, much like myself and Dr. Alex,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个有抱负的心理学家，并且正在努力成为一名临床心理学家，就像我和亚历克斯博士一样，

sentences.en: then I think you'll really find the aspiring psychologist membership helpful.
sentences.zh: 那么我想你会发现“有抱负的心理学家”会员专区非常有用。

sentences.en: You can join from just £30 a month with no minimum term.
sentences.zh: 你只需每月30英镑即可加入，没有最低期限要求。

sentences.en: There are details on screen or you can head to www.aspiring-psychologiSt.co.uk.
sentences.zh: 屏幕上有详细信息，或者你可以前往www.aspiring-psychologist.co.uk。

sentences.en: If this episode has whet your appetite for learning a little bit about trauma and how it shows up in practice, then why not head along to the episode I did about Nobody's Child,
sentences.zh: 如果这一集勾起了你了解一点创伤以及它如何在实践中表现出来的兴趣，那么为什么不去看我制作的关于《无主之子》的那一集呢？

sentences.en: which is the book by Virginia Roberts-Guffray.
sentences.zh: 那是弗吉尼亚·罗伯茨-古夫雷的书。

sentences.en: Don't forget that we've got an extra brand new episode of Psychology Actually,
sentences.zh: 别忘了我们还有《实际上是心理学》的一个全新的额外节目，

sentences.en: which is coming out midweek, coming out Wednesday evenings, both on YouTube and wherever you get your podcast on MP3.
sentences.zh: 它将在周中推出，也就是周三晚上播出，无论是在YouTube上还是在任何你能获取播客的地方都可以通过MP3收听。

sentences.en: It's called Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 它叫做《内在工作》。

sentences.en: And I think if you like the main episodes, I think you might just like the new Inner Work ones, which are now completely free.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你喜欢主节目的话，你大概也会喜欢这些全新的《内在工作》节目，现在它们是完全免费的。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你能赚到超越“用时间换金钱”的收入，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，临床心理学家，自2019年以来我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我在2022年亲自完成了该项目，此后也一直支持两批心理学家走过他们的历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励以及我独家的支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四次小组核心研讨、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南与梅森礼品以及限时一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，您必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果您有任何疑问，我随时为您解答。
